{{short description|Center of mass of a triangle's perimeter}}
{{Use American English|date=August 2020}}

In [[geometry]], the '''Spieker center''' is a special point associated with a plane [[triangle]]. It is defined as the [[center of mass]] of the [[perimeter]] of the triangle. The Spieker center of a triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} is the [[center of gravity]] of a homogeneous wire frame in the shape of {{math|△''ABC''}}.<ref name=Ross>{{cite book|last=Honsberger|first=Ross|title=Episodes in Nineteenth and Twentieth Century Euclidean Geometry|year=1995|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|pages=3–4}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Spieker center|url=http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/tcenters/class/spieker.html|accessdate=5 May 2012}}</ref> The point is named in honor of the 19th-century [[Germany|German]] [[geometer]] [[Theodor Spieker]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Spieker|first=Theodor|title=Lehrbuch der ebenen Geometrie|year=1888|location=Potsdam, Germany}}</ref> The Spieker center is a [[triangle center]] and it is listed as the point ''X''(10) in [[Clark Kimberling]]'s [[Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers]].

==Location==
[[File:SpiekerCenter.svg|thumb|350px|
'''Construction of the Spieker center.'''
{{legend|#ffe8c4|Triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend|#c4a487|[[Medial triangle]] {{math|△''DEF''}} of {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid black|[[Angle bisector]]s of {{math|△''DEF''}} ([[Concurrent lines|concurrent]] at the '''Spieker center''' {{mvar|S}})}}
{{legend-line|solid red|[[Inscribed circle]] of {{math|△''DEF''}} ([[Spieker circle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}; centered at {{mvar|S}})}}]]
The following result can be used to locate the Spieker center of any triangle.<ref name=Ross/>
:The Spieker center of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} is the [[incenter]] of the [[medial triangle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}.
That is, the Spieker center of {{math|△''ABC''}} is the center of the  circle [[inscribed]] in the [[medial triangle]] of {{math|△''ABC''}}. This circle is known as the [[Spieker circle]].

The Spieker center is also located at the intersection of the three [[Cleaver (geometry)|cleavers]] of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}. A cleaver of a triangle is a line segment that [[Bisection#Area bisectors and area-perimeter bisectors of a triangle|bisects the perimeter]] of the triangle and has one endpoint at the midpoint of one of the three sides. Each cleaver contains the center of mass of the boundary of {{math|△''ABC''}}, so the three cleavers meet at the Spieker center.

To see that the incenter of the medial triangle coincides with the intersection point of the cleavers, consider a homogeneous wireframe in the shape of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} consisting of three wires in the form of line segments having lengths {{mvar|a, b, c}}. The wire frame has the same center of mass as a system of three particles of masses {{mvar|a, b, c}} placed at the midpoints {{mvar|D, E, F}}   of the sides {{mvar|{{overline|BC}}, {{overline|CA}}, {{overline|AB}}}}. The centre of mass of the particles at {{mvar|E}} and {{mvar|F}} is the point {{mvar|P}} which divides the segment {{mvar|{{overline|EF}}}} in the ratio {{math|''c'' : ''b''}}. The line {{mvar|DP}}  is the internal bisector of {{math|∠''D''}}. The centre of mass of the three particle system thus lies on the internal bisector of {{math|∠''D''}}. Similar arguments show that the center mass of the three particle system lies on the internal bisectors of {{math|∠''E''}} and {{math|∠''F''}} also. It follows that the center of mass of the wire frame is the point of concurrence of the internal bisectors of the angles of the triangle  {{math|△''DEF''}} , which is the incenter of the medial triangle  {{math|△''DEF''}} .

==Properties==
[[File:CleavanceCenter.svg|thumb|350px|The Spieker center of a triangle is the cleavance center of the triangle.
{{legend|#ffe8c4|Triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|dashed #333333|Angle bisectors of {{math|△''ABC''}} (concurrent at the [[incenter]] {{mvar|I}})}}
{{legend-line|solid blue|[[Cleaver (geometry)|Cleavers]] of {{math|△''ABC''}} (concurrent at the '''Spieker center''' {{mvar|S}})}}
{{legend|#c4a487|[[Medial triangle]] {{math|△''DEF''}} of {{math|△''ABC''}}}}
{{legend-line|solid red|Inscribed circle of {{math|△''DEF''}} (Spieker circle of {{math|△''ABC''}}; centered at {{mvar|S}})}}]]
Let {{mvar|S}} be the Spieker center of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}.
*The [[trilinear coordinates]] of {{mvar|S}} are
:: <math>bc(b+c) : ca(c+a) : ab(a+b).</math><ref name=Clark>{{cite web|last=Kimberling|first=Clark|title=Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers|url= http://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/ETC.html|accessdate=5 May 2012}}</ref>
*The [[barycentric coordinate system (mathematics)|barycentric coordinates]] of {{mvar|S}}  are
:: <math>b+c : c+a : a+b.</math><ref  name=Clark/>
*{{mvar|S}} is the [[Power center (geometry)|radical center]] of the three [[excircle]]s.<ref>{{citation|title=Some triangle centers associated with the circles tangent to the excircles|journal=Forum Geometricorum|url=http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2010volume10/FG201006.pdf|volume=10|year=2010|pages=35–40|first=Boris|last=Odenhal|access-date=2014-11-30|archive-date=2021-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211114125342/https://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2010volume10/FG201006.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*{{mvar|S}} is the  [[Cleaver (geometry)|cleavance center]] of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} <ref name=Ross/>
*{{mvar|S}} is [[collinear]] with the [[incenter]] ({{mvar|I}}), the [[centroid]] ({{mvar|G}}), and the  [[Nagel point]] ({{mvar|M}}) of triangle {{math|△''ABC''}}. Moreover,<ref>{{cite web|last=Bogomolny|first=A.|authorlink= Alexander Bogomolny |title=Nagel Line from Interactive Mathematics Miscellany and Puzzles|url=http://www.cut-the-knot.org/Curriculum/Geometry/NagelLine.shtml|accessdate=5 May 2012}}</ref>
::<math>IS= SM, \quad IG= 2 \cdot GS, \quad MG= 2\cdot IG.</math>
:Thus on a suitably scaled and positioned number line, {{math|1=''I'' = 0}}, {{math|1=''G'' = 2}}, {{math|1=''S'' = 3}}, and {{math|1=''M'' = 6}}.
*{{mvar|S}}  lies on the [[Kiepert conics|Kiepert hyperbola]]. {{mvar|S}} is the point of concurrence of the lines {{mvar|AX, BY, CZ}} where {{math|△''XBC'', △''YCA'', △''ZAB''}} are similar, isosceles and similarly situated triangles  constructed on the sides of  triangle {{math|△''ABC''}} as bases, having the common base angle<ref>{{mathworld|title=Kiepert Hyperbola|urlname=KiepertHyperbola}}</ref>
:: <math>\theta = \tan^{-1}\left[ \tan\left(\frac{A}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{B}{2}\right) \tan\left(\frac{C}{2}\right) \right].</math>
